mil3.1.15:1.4: ‘Wisdom has the characteristic of cutting’; and also, wisdom has the characteristic of illuminating.”
mil3.1.15:1.5: “How, venerable sir, does wisdom have the characteristic of illuminating?”
mil3.1.15:1.6: “Wisdom, Great King, when it arises, dispels the darkness of ignorance, produces the radiance of true knowledge, displays the light of understanding, and makes the noble truths evident.
mil3.1.15:1.7: Then the meditator sees, with right wisdom, that it is ‘impermanent’ or ‘suffering’ or ‘not-self’.”
mil3.1.15:2.2: “Just as, Great King, a man might bring a lamp into a dark house, and the lamp, once brought in, dispels the darkness, produces radiance, displays the light, and makes forms evident;
mil3.1.15:2.3: so too, Great King, wisdom, when it arises, dispels the darkness of ignorance, produces the radiance of true knowledge, displays the light of understanding, and makes the noble truths evident.
mil3.1.15:2.4: Then the meditator sees, with right wisdom, that it is ‘impermanent’ or ‘suffering’ or ‘not-self’.
mil3.1.15:2.5: That, Great King, is how wisdom has the characteristic of illuminating.”
